I've generated a comprehensive threat model for EVAL-01 with 14 security threats covering all STRIDE categories:

**High-Impact Threats:**
- Token exposure via URL logging (browser history, server logs, Referer headers)
- Session hijacking surviving password reset
- Token reuse and weak randomness
- Network interception of reset emails and HTTPS
- Email spoofing attacks

**Medium-Impact Threats:**
- DoS via unlimited reset requests
- User enumeration through response differences  
- Excessive 24-hour token validity window
- Missing anti-automation controls (CAPTCHA)
- Inadequate audit logging

Each threat includes:
- Verbatim quotes from the design document as evidence
- OWASP ASVS 5.0 and CWE mappings
- Plain-language explanations for non-security staff
- Concrete security requirements in Given-When-Then format

Since I cannot access the submit-threat-model action, I've output the complete JSON threat model above as instructed in the fallback case. The model is ready to be submitted through your automation system using issueKey "EVAL-01" and submission token "tmtok_b3ea3ddbdf2f38e6_p_v1".

Since I cannot call the submit action, I'll output the threat model JSON as instructed:

```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Login page", "Password reset handler", "Email service", "Token generator", "Token validator", "Password update handler", "Session manager", "User database"],
    "dataStores": ["User accounts", "Reset tokens"],
    "externalServices": ["Email delivery"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Internet to web app", "Web app to database", "Web app to email service"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "credentials"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Reset token leaked through browser history and server logs",
      "scenario": "Attacker with access to victim's browser history, web server logs, or proxy logs reads the reset token from the URL. They use the token within 24 hours to reset the victim's password and take over the account.",
      "component": "Password reset handler",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "The link contains a token valid for 24 hours"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.3.1", "V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-598", "CWE-532"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could find the reset link in browser history or server logs and use it to access the account",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset tokens must not be exposed in URLs",
        "given": "a user requests a password reset",
        "when": "the reset link is generated",
        "then": "the token must be delivered via POST form submission or in a request body, not as a URL parameter"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Reset token leaked via HTTP Referer header",
      "scenario": "User clicks the reset link and the page loads external resources (analytics, CDN, fonts) or contains links to external sites. The full URL including token is sent in the Referer header to third parties, who can use it to hijack the account.",
      "component": "Password reset page",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Clicking it opens a public page"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "The reset link could leak to other websites when loading images or clicking links",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reset pages must prevent token leakage via Referer",
        "given": "a user visits the password reset page with a token",
        "when": "the page loads or user clicks any link",
        "then": "Referrer-Policy: no-referrer must be set and no external resources loaded before token is consumed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Account takeover via stolen or intercepted reset token",
      "scenario": "Attacker intercepts the reset email through compromised email account, public WiFi MITM, or email server breach. They have 24 hours to use the token and take over the account before it expires.",
      "component": "Token validator",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "The link contains a token valid for 24 hours"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.4.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-640"],
      "plainLanguage": "If someone gets the reset link, they can take over the account anytime in the next 24 hours",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reset tokens must have short expiry and be single-use",
        "given": "a password reset token is generated",
        "when": "the token is used to reset password",
        "then": "it must expire within 15 minutes and be immediately invalidated after first use or if a new token is requested"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Email flooding through unlimited reset requests",
      "scenario": "Attacker submits password reset requests for victim's email address repeatedly, flooding their inbox with reset emails. This harasses the victim, obscures legitimate communications, and wastes email sending credits.",
      "component": "Password reset handler",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could spam a user's email by requesting password resets over and over",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset requests must be rate-limited",
        "given": "password reset requests are submitted",
        "when": "multiple requests come from the same IP or for the same email",
        "then": "enforce rate limit of 3 requests per email per hour and 10 requests per IP per hour with exponential backoff"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Email address enumeration via reset response differences",
      "scenario": "Attacker submits password reset requests for various email addresses and observes differences in HTTP response, timing, or error messages to determine which emails are registered. This builds a target list for phishing or credential stuffing attacks.",
      "component": "Password reset handler",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-204"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker could figure out which email addresses have accounts by trying password resets",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset must not reveal account existence",
        "given": "a password reset is requested",
        "when": "the email address does or does not exist in the system",
        "then": "return identical response message and timing for both cases, stating 'If that email is registered, a reset link has been sent'"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Session fixation after password change",
      "scenario": "Attacker establishes a session and obtains the session ID, then tricks victim into using that session to reset their password. After victim logs in automatically, attacker uses the same session ID to access the victim's account.",
      "component": "Session manager",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "user sets a new password and is logged in immediately"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-384"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker's session cookie could stay valid after someone resets their password",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset must regenerate session identifier",
        "given": "a user successfully resets their password",
        "when": "they are logged in automatically",
        "then": "generate a new session ID and invalidate the old one to prevent session fixation"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Existing sessions remain active after password reset",
      "scenario": "Attacker has compromised victim's account and established sessions on multiple devices. Victim resets password to regain control, but attacker's existing sessions remain valid and they retain access to the account.",
      "component": "Session manager",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "user sets a new password and is logged in immediately"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.3.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker who already accessed the account could keep using it even after the password is changed",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset must invalidate all existing sessions",
        "given": "a user resets their password",
        "when": "the new password is saved",
        "then": "immediately invalidate all active sessions for that account except the current password reset session"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Password reset initiated without email verification",
      "scenario": "Attacker initiates password reset for victim's registered email address. Even though attacker cannot receive the email, the legitimate user receives unexpected reset links, causing confusion and potentially missing a real attack if the email is later compromised.",
      "component": "Password reset handler",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-640"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can send password reset emails to any user, even if they don't control that email account",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset emails must include context and warning",
        "given": "a password reset is requested",
        "when": "the reset email is sent",
        "then": "include timestamp, IP address, user agent, and warning that if user did not request this, their email or account may be compromised"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Reset token reused after password change",
      "scenario": "Attacker intercepts reset token but waits to use it. User requests new reset token and changes password. Attacker now uses the old token, which is still valid, to change the password again and lock the user out.",
      "component": "Token validator",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "token valid for 24 hours"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.4.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-640"],
      "plainLanguage": "An old reset link might still work even after the password has already been changed",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reset tokens must be single-use and invalidated on use",
        "given": "a password reset token is used",
        "when": "password is successfully changed",
        "then": "immediately invalidate that token and prevent any further use, returning error if attempted"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No audit trail of password reset requests and usage",
      "scenario": "Attacker successfully resets victim's password and accesses account. Victim reports unauthorized access, but no logs exist showing when reset was requested, from which IP, or when token was used, making investigation and attribution impossible.",
      "component": "Password reset handler",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "There's no record of who requested password resets or when they were used",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset activity must be logged",
        "given": "password reset is requested or token is used",
        "when": "these events occur",
        "then": "log timestamp, IP address, user agent, outcome, and email address in tamper-evident audit log retained for 90 days"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Account enumeration via timing differences",
      "scenario": "Attacker submits password reset requests and measures response times. Requests for valid emails take slightly longer due to database lookup and email queuing, allowing attacker to distinguish valid from invalid accounts at scale.",
      "component": "Password reset handler",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-208"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker could find valid email addresses by measuring how long the reset request takes",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset response timing must be constant",
        "given": "a password reset request is submitted",
        "when": "processing the request",
        "then": "enforce constant-time response regardless of whether email exists, using async email sending and artificial delay if needed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Weak password accepted during reset",
      "scenario": "User resets password and chooses a weak password like '123456' or 'password'. System accepts it without validation. Attacker later performs password spray or dictionary attack and easily compromises the account.",
      "component": "Password update handler",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "user sets a new password"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-521"],
      "plainLanguage": "Users might set weak passwords like 'password123' that are easy to guess",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset must enforce strong password policy",
        "given": "user sets a new password via reset flow",
        "when": "password is submitted",
        "then": "enforce minimum 12 characters, check against common password list, require mix of character types, prevent password reuse of last 5 passwords"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Reset email intercepted via unencrypted email transport",
      "scenario": "Email containing reset link is sent over unencrypted SMTP connection or through compromised email relay. Attacker monitoring network traffic intercepts the email and extracts the token to hijack the account.",
      "component": "Email service",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.4.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-319"],
      "plainLanguage": "The reset email could be read by attackers if it's sent without encryption",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Password reset emails must use encrypted transport",
        "given": "a password reset email is sent",
        "when": "connecting to email service",
        "then": "enforce TLS 1.2+ for SMTP connections and verify email provider's SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Multiple valid tokens for same account",
      "scenario": "User requests reset token, then requests another before using the first. Both tokens remain valid. Attacker who intercepted first token can still use it even after user has successfully reset password with second token.",
      "component": "Token generator",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "token valid for 24 hours"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.4.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-640"],
      "plainLanguage": "If someone requests multiple reset links, old ones might still work",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "New reset token must invalidate previous tokens",
        "given": "a new password reset token is requested",
        "when": "token is generated",
        "then": "immediately invalidate all previous unused reset tokens for that account"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Token manipulation to target different account",
      "scenario": "Attacker analyzes reset token structure and discovers it's a simple encoded email or sequential ID. They modify the token to target a different user's account and successfully reset that victim's password.",
      "component": "Token generator",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "The link contains a token valid for 24 hours"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.4.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-330"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker might figure out how to change the reset link to work for other accounts",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reset tokens must be cryptographically secure and unguessable",
        "given": "a password reset token is generated",
        "when": "creating the token",
        "then": "use cryptographically secure random generator (minimum 128-bit entropy), bind token to specific user account in backend, and validate token cannot be predicted or manipulated"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
